title: first quotient normalization.
statement:
variable (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
  [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (S : Scheme.{u})

theorem signedTwistFirstReduction (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ b : SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsOfUniverses.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
        (completedIntegralCommRingProjectionUnrestricted l E S n)
        (purTwistIntegralModule S l E) ≅ purTwistFiniteOne S l E n,
      ∀ (U : S.ProEtᵒᵖ) (x : (purTwistIntegralModule S l E).val.obj U),
        b.hom.val.app U (SheafOfModules.scalarExtensionSection
          (completedIntegralCommRingProjectionUnrestricted l E S n)
          (purTwistIntegralModule S l E) U 1 x) =
          ((((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
            (𝟙 (integralCoefficientSheaf l E S n).obj)).unit.app
              (SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsPresheafOfUniverses.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
                (purTwistIntegralQuotient S l E n) (purTwistIntegralOne S l E))).app U)
            ((1 : (integralCoefficientSheaf l E S n).obj.obj U) ⊗ₜ[
              (purTwistIntegralConstant S l E).obj.obj U,
              ((purTwistIntegralQuotient S l E n).hom.app U).hom] x))

proof.text: The completed first-line action restricts to the prescribed constant action. The explicit identity-on-sections isomorphism integralForgetIso identifies this restriction with the original integral root tensor line.

proof.text: The completion map and finite quotient map satisfy the coefficient triangle. Their sectionwise kernels are generated by the same uniformizer power. quotientRestrictionHomEquiv therefore makes restriction followed by quotient extension a left adjoint to completed quotient restriction. Compare it with tensorAdjunction by leftAdjointUniq.

proof.text: Take the inverse comparison and then extend integralForgetIso. The unit identity for leftAdjointUniq and naturality of the module-sheafification unit give exactly the prescribed section 1 tensor x. Pure tensors determine the morphism, including empty sites and zero rings.
